guarantees.claim: addr_sel always equals the bit-slice tlram_addr[StateAddrW+:SelAddrW].
When int'(addr_sel) < Share, tlram_rdata_endian is assigned muxed_state[addr_sel]; otherwise tlram_rdata_endian is assigned 0.

assumptions.claim: The bus width of tlram_addr must be at least StateAddrW + SelAddrW so that the part-select tlram_addr[StateAddrW+:SelAddrW] stays in bounds.
assumptions.risk: An out-of-bounds part-select would produce a corrupted or X addr_sel, breaking downstream address decoding.

assumptions.claim: The parameter Share must not exceed the bit-width of muxed_state, ensuring that addr_sel < Share implies addr_sel is a legal index into muxed_state.
assumptions.risk: If Share > $bits(muxed_state), a legal addr_sel value (<Share) could still be out-of-range, causing an out-of-bounds bit-select on muxed_state (X propagation/simulation error).

uncertain_points.claim: If Share > $bits(muxed_state), the guard int'(addr_sel) < Share does not prevent out-of-bounds indexing when addr_sel is in the range [$bits(muxed_state), Share-1].
uncertain_points.cond: when Share > $bits(muxed_state) and addr_sel in that range
uncertain_points.risk: Illegal read of muxed_state may propagate X or unknown data into tlram_rdata_endian, potentially affecting downstream logic.

uncertain_points.claim: The meaning of forcing tlram_rdata_endian to 0 when addr_sel >= Share is not documented; it may be an address‑space hole but could hide a fault or mask unintentional reads.
uncertain_points.risk: A silent zero return may conceal a design error or security‑relevant signal, and it is unclear whether this behavior is intentional or accidental.
